issues.problem: Public SODA reads require no authentication. A Socrata app token identifies the application for throttling and is explicitly not necessarily an authentication credential, so classifying the API as apiKey is misleading.
issues.suggestion: Use type "none" and explain that an optional X-App-Token can provide a separate application request pool.

issues.problem: The historical approximately 1,000-requests-per-hour anonymous figure is not a documented current limit. Socrata currently leaves the anonymous threshold unspecified and says token-bearing requests are generally unthrottled unless abusive or malicious.
issues.suggestion: Remove the historical number and state that anonymous requests have an unpublished lower limit while app-token requests are subject to abuse controls.

issues.problem: Because the URL is double-quoted, the shell expands $limit as an environment variable, usually turning the query into ?=5 instead of sending the SODA $limit parameter.
issues.suggestion: Use single quotes around the URL or escape the dollar sign, for example: curl -H "X-App-Token: YOUR_API_KEY" 'https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/erm2-nwe9.json?$limit=5'.

issues.problem: The documented interface uses the api-key query parameter. The claim that some endpoints accept X-Api-Key is not supported by the NYT API specifications and may be a conflation with other API gateways.
issues.suggestion: State only that the key is supplied through the api-key query parameter unless a specific NYT endpoint with documented header support is identified.

issues.problem: The statement "not published" is incorrect; the NYT developer FAQ publishes default call limits.
issues.suggestion: Use the currently documented limits, commonly 500 requests per day and 5 requests per minute per API, and recheck the developer dashboard for endpoint-specific overrides.

issues.problem: "unknown" omits the published request ceilings and the material limitation that ordinary developer access is intended for non-commercial use; commercial redistribution or higher-volume use requires an agreement with NYT.
issues.suggestion: Record the current developer quota and note the non-commercial-use/licensing restriction; verify any monthly aggregate quota directly in the current developer portal.

issues.problem: Okta publishes concrete Integrator Free Plan limits, so "unknown" obscures material restrictions. The plan is capped at 10 active users and 5 Workflows and may deactivate after 180 consecutive days without a user sign-in unless an app is submitted to the OIN.
issues.suggestion: Replace "unknown" with the current Integrator Free Plan limits and inactivity condition.

issues.problem: A null value incorrectly suggests that Okta has no paid offerings. Okta sells paid Workforce Identity and Customer Identity products.
issues.suggestion: State that paid commercial plans are available, with pricing and API capacity varying by product, licenses, and add-ons; link or refer users to current Okta pricing or sales.

issues.problem: The description advertises autocomplete as a normal capability, but Open Brewery DB has deprecated its autocomplete endpoint and announced its removal from v1 by the end of 2026.
issues.suggestion: Remove autocomplete from the advertised capabilities or explicitly mark it deprecated and direct users to the supported brewery search endpoint.

issues.problem: The value is the website origin rather than the current recommended API root. Open Food Facts now recommends API v3, currently v3.6, for new integrations; v2 is deprecated.
issues.suggestion: Use https://world.openfoodfacts.org/api/v3.6 for new integrations, or explicitly identify the existing value as an origin rather than a versioned API base.

issues.problem: The listed approximately 100 product requests per minute and 2 facet requests per minute are stale. Current official documentation states 15 product-read requests per minute per IP and 10 search requests per minute per IP.
issues.suggestion: Replace the value with the currently published 15 product reads/minute/IP and 10 searches/minute/IP, plus the documented global abuse limits and bulk-download guidance.

issues.problem: The example uses API v2, which is now officially deprecated, although still supported for backward compatibility.
issues.suggestion: For a new directory example, use the current v3.6 product endpoint and update the response snippet to its schema; retain v2 only if clearly labeled deprecated.

issues.problem: The claim that limits are not published is false. Open Library publishes a default limit of 1 request per second and 3 requests per second for identified requests carrying an application User-Agent and contact information.
issues.suggestion: Set the rate limit to 1 request/second anonymously and 3 requests/second when properly identified, and mention the low-volume and no-bulk-backend usage guidelines.
